1. दिक्क ifc. = 2. दिश्.
2. दिक्क m. = करभ (v.l. धिक्क and विक्क), W.
&c. See under 2. दिश्.
दिक्—कन्या f. a quarter of the sky deified as a young virgin, Bhartṛ. iii, 93 (v.l. कान्ता).
in comp. for 2. दिश्, p. 480.
दिक्—कर mf(ई)n. youthful, juvenile (lit. making, i.e. changing q˚ continually, restless)
दिक्—कर m. a youth, L.
= अरुण (as making a q˚ for the sun), L.
= सम्भु (granter of space, promoter?), L.
दिक्—करी f. a young woman, L.
दिक्—कर—वासिनी f. a form of Devī, VP.

दिक्—करिक mfn. (ifc.) = -करिन् and (at, once) = -करिका f. the mark of a bite or of a nail, Śiś. iv, 29^1
[1] Correction submitted by Scott Rhodes on 20260703. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/285.
दिक्—करिका f. N. of a river, KālP.
दिक्—करिन् m. ‘elephant of the q˚’, one of the mythical elephants which stand in the four or eight quarters of the sky and support the earth, BhP.
दिक्—कान्ता (Bhartṛ. iii, 93) f. = -कन्या.
दिक्—कामिनी f. (Rājat. iii, 382) = -कन्या.
दिक्—कुञ्जर m. = -करिन्, Sāh.
दिक्—कुमार m. pl. ‘the youths of the q˚’, a class of deities (with Jainas), L.
दिक्—चक्र n. the circuit of the q˚ of the compass, the horizon, Ratn. iii, 5
the compass, the whole world, VarBṛS.
दिक्—चक्र—वाल n. the whole range of sight, the scenery all around, Kād.
दिक्—छब्द (for शब्द) m. a word denoting a direction, Pāṇ. ii, 3, 29.
दिक्—तट m. the line of the horizon, remotest distance, Rājat.; Kathās.
दिक्—त॑स् ind. from the regions of the sky, ŚBr.
दिक्—तुल्य mfn. having the same direction, Sūryas.
दिक्—तुल्य—ता f., ib.
दिक्—पति m. a regent or guardian of a q˚ of the sky (often identified with लोक-पाल, q.v.), VarBṛS.; Gīt.
दिक्—पथ m. ‘the path of the horizon’, the surrounding region or q˚, Rājat. v, 341.
दिक्—पाल m. = -पति, Rājat. iv, 225.
praise of the guardians of the world (a kind of introductory ceremony).
दिक्—प्रविभाग m. a q˚, direction Sch. on VarBṛS.
दिक्—प्रेक्षण n. looking round in all directions (from fear &c.), Sāh.
दिक्—शूल n. ‘sky-spear’, any inauspicious planetary conjunction
N. of partic. days on which it is not allowed to travel in certain directions, L.
दिक्—शूल—लक्षण n. N. of ch. of the PSarv.
दिक्—सम mfn. = -तुल्य, Sūryas.
दिक्—साधन-यन्त्र n. N. of wk.
दिक्—साम्य n. sameness of direction, Sūryas.
दिक्—सुदृश् (SŚaṃkar.) and दिक्—सुन्दरी (Gīt.), f. = -कन्या
दिक्—सुदृश् (SŚaṃkar.) and दिक्—सुन्दरी (Gīt.), f. = -कन्या
दिक्—स्रक्ति mfn. having the angles or corners towards the quarters of the compass Sch. on KātyŚr.
दिक्—स्वामिन् m. = -पति, VarBṛS.
a priest, spiritual guide
N. of a king, Vīrac.
consecrating one's self or causing one's self to be consecrated, consecration, initiation, ŚrS.; MBh.
id., VarBṛS. xcviii, 14.
दीक्˚षणी॑य mfn. (fr. √ दिक्ष्) to be consecrated or initiated
relating to consecration, Br.
दीक्˚षणी॑या f. (Vait.) = ˚येष्टि f. the sacrifice of consecration or initiation, Br.; ŚrS.
L. m. consecrator, AitBr. i, 4
preparation or consecration for a religious ceremony, undertaking religious observances for a partic. purpose and the observances themselves, AV.; VS.; Br.; ŚrS. &c.
dedication, initiation (personified as the wife of Soma,
, of Rudra Ugra or R˚ Vāmadeva, Pur.)
any serious preparation (as for battle), MBh.; Hariv.; Kāv.
self-devotion to a person or god, complete resignation or restriction to, exclusive occupation with (comp.; cf. विरह-, शाक-, शृङ्गार.).
दीक्षा—करण n. performance of consecration, Sarvad.
दीक्षा—कारिन् mfn. consecrating, initiating, ib.
दीक्षा—क्रम-रत्न n. ‘the jewel of the regular order of initiation’, N. of wk.
दीक्षा—गुरु m. a teacher of initiation, Bālar. x, 41.
दीक्षा˚ङ्ग-स्वस्ति-वाचन (˚क्षाङ्ग्˚) n. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—तत्त्व n. ‘essence of initiation’, N. of wk.
दीक्षा˚न्त (˚क्ष्तान्˚) m. the end of a D˚ = अवभृथ, L.
दीक्षा॑—पति (˚क्षा॑-), m. ‘consecration-lord’, i.e. Soma, VS. v, 6.
दीक्षा—पत्त्र n. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—पद्धति f. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—पा॑ल m. guardian of initiation (Agni or Viṣṇu), Br.
दीक्षा—प्रकरण n. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—फल n. ‘the fruit of initiation’, N. of a ch. of the PSarv.
दीक्षा—मय mf(ई)n. consisting in initiation,
Hariv. 2115
दीक्षा—महोत्सव m. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—मासादि-विचार m. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—रत्न n. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—विधान n. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—विधि m. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—विनोद m. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—विवेक m. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—संस्कार m. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—सूक्त n. N. of wk.
दीक्षा—सेतु m. N. of wk.
mf(ई, GopBr. i, 5, 24)n. consecrated, initiated into (dat. loc. instr., or comp.), AV.; TS.; Br.; ŚrS.; Mn.; MBh. &c.
prepared, ready for (dat. instr. or comp.), MBh.; R. (˚तं-√ कृ, to initiate, instruct, Kathās. xx, 198)
performed (as the Dīkṣā ceremony), W.
a priest engaged in a D˚ (-त्व n., Jaim.)

a pupil of (affixed, and rarely prefixed to the N. of a teacher, and given as a N. to a Brāhman to denote his being a pupil of that t˚, e.g. भट्टोजि-, शं-कर-; sometimes the teacher's N. is dropped and D˚ is used alone).
दीक्षित॑—त्व n., Jaim.
दीक्षित—धुण्ढि-राज m. N. of men, Cat.
दीक्षित—बाल-कृष्ण m. N. of men, Cat.
दीक्षित—यज्ञदत्त m. N. of men, Cat.
दीक्षित—वसन n. the garment of an initiated person, ŚBr.
दीक्षित—वाद॑ m. the statement that a person is initiated, TS.
दीक्षित—विमित॑ n. a temporary dwelling for a person about to be initiated, Kāṭh. xiii, 1; AitBr. i, 3 (cf. प्राचीन-वंश).
दीक्षित—व्रत n. the vow of an initiated person, KātyŚr. iv, 6, 13.
दीक्षित—सामराज m. N. of the author of Dhūrta-nartaka.
= ˚त-वाद, Vait. xi, 12.
N. of the wife of Dīkṣitayajñadatta, L.
दीक्षि˚तीय mfn. written by a Dīkṣita
दीक्षि˚तीय n. N. of such a work.
a consecrator, Pāṇ. iii, 2, 153.
one who has been initiated (cf. गण-).
